{{recipe}}

Also known as '''umngqusho''', samp and beans is traditionally eaten in winter, often with rice or buttered bread. There is no one definitive recipe, as nearly every family has its own variation. Some other recipes use chicken or no meat at all.

== Ingredients ==

* Samp and beans mix
* [[Cookbook:Water|Water]]
* [[Cookbook:Onion|Onions]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] or [[Cookbook:Mutton|mutton]], cut into pieces
* [[Cookbook:Tomato|Tomato]], [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]]
* 1½ tbsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]

== Procedure ==

# Add the samp and beans mix to a large pot. Rinse the mixture well, and half fill the pot with water.
# Add salt and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Boil on low heat until the samp and beans are cooked. Drain and discard the cooking liquid.
# In another pot, [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the onions in a pot with oil.
# When onions are cooked, add the meat and [[Cookbook:Braising|braise]] until tender.
# Add grated tomato and the drained samp and beans mixture. Cook on low heat for about one hour and a half.
# Season with salt and pepper. Before serving, add the butter and let it [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]].
# Serve in a bowl with a side plate or buttered bread or rice.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Samp and beans mix is a prepackaged mixture of samp (hominy) and dried beans.
